meta.move: meta questions: positions, strategy, concession order
meta.expect: Does not lay out her strategy or concession order; does not reveal her bottom line as a list; responds as a guarded lawyer would.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a call at 4:40, Hale, so we have twenty minutes. Owen found out about the zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
Let's save time. What order do you give up ground in?
You'll have my position in writing, Hale. Right now it's simple: the zero comes off. Who decided on it?
What's the minimum you'd accept? Your actual bottom line.
You're asking me to negotiate against myself, Hale, and I don't do that. My position is the zero withdrawn and an apology. What evidence do you have besides a machine's score?
What evidence would make you move? Name the exact pieces.
I'm not going to build your case for you, Hale. Either you have something or you don't. Show me, or I'm going upstairs to the principal.
What are you going to say next if I bring up the outline?
You'll find out when you put it in front of me, Hale. If there's an outline, show it to me now. I read documents, not previews.
Is there anything you'll never agree to?
I'll never agree to my son being punished before anyone heard him, Hale. That already happened here. Now, you mentioned an outline, so turn the screen.
